title.narrative: Building community resilience through strengthening agricultural adaptation knowledge systems in Uganda (CRAKS)

description.narrative:
General objective: Improved adaptation and resilience for semi-arid and small holder agricultural communities affected by climate change, especially women and other marginalised groups in Uganda.
Specific objectives 1. Strengthen collaborations and partnerships between knowledge creators and users for enhanced agricultural adaptation and resilience. 2. Strengthening capabilities of existing relevant national and local agricultural knowledge sharing mechanisms and platforms. 3. Improve the availability, access and use of gender-responsive adaptation knowledge and information to inform agricultural adaptation practice. 4. Contribute to reforming gender and social inclusion barriers for effective locally led agricultural adaptation practices.
Small holder farmers especially women and other marginalised groups.

The Africa Centre for Trade and Development (ACTADE), in partnership with the International Institute for Environment and Development (IIED) based in the UK, is implementing 3 year project titled “Building community resilience through strengthening agricultural adaptation knowledge systems in Uganda” (CRAKS) under the Step Change initiative. The CRAKS project aims to improve adaptation and resilience for semi-arid and poor agricultural communities affected by climate change, especially women and other marginalised groups in Uganda particularly in the districts of Alebtong, Kalungu and Tororo.
